name: Data table
summary: A plain table of up to 50 rows with a title and a summary line, sortable by any column and shown ten rows to a page.
use: for a list of records an assistant or a report fills in, such as invoices, orders or transactions
states: first column fixed on a phone
a11y: A real table with column headers; each header is a button that sorts the rows and announces the order through aria-sort, and the page range is a status line.

use_when: an answer that lists records with the same few fields, where the person may want to sort or page through them
avoid_when: two to four headline totals: use kpi-strip
numbers over time: use line-chart or bar-chart
a handful of options to pick from: use result-list or comparison
rows the person must select and act on in bulk: use receipts-table

parts.name: summary
parts.what: one line under the title: counts, totals or the date range

parts.name: columns
parts.what: one column: its label and alignment; the script draws the header row from these, each header a button that sorts by it

parts.name: cells
parts.what: one cell's text, in column order

parts.name: more_note
parts.what: a note when there are more records than the table shows

parts.name: pager
parts.what: the page range and Previous and Next, shown when there are more than ten rows

empty.how: with no rows the renderer adds one quiet line saying there is nothing to show, drawn across the table under the headers; the pager stays hidden

loading.how: the Smart UI renderer draws each marked slot as a quiet block of its size while the data arrives; the static file shows the filled part

error.how: if the records fail to load, show error-retry in place of the table

disabled.how: Previous is disabled on the first page and Next on the last

overflow.how: more than ten rows page ten at a time; wide tables scroll sideways in their own box with the first column fixed on a phone

long_text.how: a long cell wraps at about 14rem and breaks long words, so a row grows taller instead of wider

keyboard: Tab reaches each column header, then Previous and Next
Enter or Space on a header sorts by that column; again reverses the order
